summary: After 3 iterations optimizing a branch-and-bound solver for a bounded knapsack problem, we've reached a mean score of 99.0 (80% of runs score 100, 20% score 95). The algorithm finds exact optimal solutions in <25ms locally, but Docker container overhead occasionally pushes total wall time past the 1-second limit, causing ~20% of runs to fall back to a heuristic solution scoring 95.
key_points: Iteration 1 built a B&B solver with Lagrangian relaxation bounds that finds exact optima on all 20 test cases locally. Iteration 2 discovered Docker timing variance causes 30% failure rate (TLE); a CPU-time guard using clock() didn't help because Docker overhead is wall-time. Iteration 3 added a wall-time guard (chrono::steady_clock, amortized every 512 nodes) which improved reliability from 70% → 80% at score 100 and mean from 98.5 → 99.0.

Key constraint: the algorithm itself runs in <25ms, but Docker container startup and scheduling add 300-500ms of irreducible overhead. The 700ms wall-time guard leaves 300ms for this overhead, but ~20% of the time Docker takes longer. Further algorithmic speedups have diminishing returns since the algorithm is already very fast.

Critical technical findings: (1) per-node chrono calls double execution time — must amortize to every 512 nodes; (2) tight Lagrangian bounds at B&B levels 0-7 are essential — removing them causes all test cases to timeout; (3) 12 ternary search iterations for bounds is optimal — reducing to 8 makes some cases 4x slower; (4) fast I/O (fread/printf) is necessary — string/istringstream/cout negate speed gains.

Remaining unknowns: Can the 20% failure rate be reduced further? Possible approaches for next iteration: (a) lower the wall-time guard threshold (e.g., 500ms) to force earlier fallback to heuristic, trading occasional optimality for reliability; (b) try a completely different fast approach (scaled DP) that might be more predictable in timing; (c) improve the greedy/local-search fallback so it scores closer to 100 even when B&B times out.

Recommendation: CONTINUE. The score is already very high (99.0 mean), but there may be room to push toward a consistent 100 by either making the fallback solution better (so 95→100 when B&B times out) or by further reducing algorithm time to leave more margin for Docker overhead.
